NOTE.—Following the program, a meeting will be held in the school building for all former Savoy College students or friends interested who may be present to consider plans for a reunion of the students on or about November 1.

COMMITTEE MEETINGS.—Although the building program was delayed by the war situation, Mr. Thomasson's dedication address quoted later in this chapter, plans for a Savoy College Reunion at its completion went on with growing enthusiasm. The general committee, in working up plans for the reunion, held at the homes of the members some "five little reunions" before the final one. The five meetings prior to the big Reunion of August 13, 1938, were:

June 5, 1938, at Mr. Gus W. Thomasson's, 4502 Rawlins Avenue, Dallas.
June 26, 1938, at Mrs. Kate King Montgomery's, Pittsburgh, Texas.
July 3, 1938, at Mrs. Ora Lindsay Stinnett's, 811 Monroe Street, Commerce, Texas.
July 17, 1938, at Judge Mason's, Clark's, Greenville, Texas.
July 31, 1938, at Mrs. J. B. May's, Savoy, Texas.

Their cordiality was such that each welcomed the others and the committee members, as they expressed it, had fun among themselves far above and beyond the duties of the work. Excerpts from a few letters are quoted below just as a sample of their "preliminary pleasures":

Dear Old Savoy friends:
I am enclosing herewith copies of letters from Harlow Roberts and Albert Galbraith concerning the proposed Savoy College School reunion and am particularly directing your attention to what is said about the boys headed for a camp to be organized to protect us from Mr. Hitler. I haven't read much that is pathetic about the love but it may be mostly in their heads
